title: Publishing a repository is a separate choice
when: Project creation, clone, existing-folder adoption or later publication
need: A prepared Git repository can stay local. Skipping GitHub makes the publish prompt default to No — keep it local; a verified connection keeps Yes — publish to GitHub selected. Connecting GitHub does not require publishing every project. Clone and adoption share an explicit publication destination choice: read-only preserves fetching and disables Yoke publication through the checkout publication_read_only project setting; Git remotes and native Git behavior stay unchanged; legacy disabled push URLs migrate once to this setting and only those legacy values are removed; source writes state confirmed versus unverified access; Fork and Duplicate use supported owned destinations. Publication-required work refuses read-only destinations before lane preparation. Repeated setup reopens the same destination choice for a read-only project and preserves a configured writable project.
gap: JOURNEYS 4–5 currently makes pushing to GitHub sound mandatory. That edge should be reviewed against the supported keep-local path.
review: Explicit CLI publication choices must survive adopting a checkout and setting up a separate project after an existing match. Duplicate collects visibility, owner and repository before Review; Review and Apply use that destination while retaining source identity. Installed Duplicate acceptance remains owed after the shared mission found this route skipped destination selection.
